# Plan: Add an optional formal mode to render()

## Goal
`render(user, { formal: true })` returns `"Dear <name>"`. The one-argument call keeps returning `"Hi <name>"` exactly as before, and the existing test must keep passing unchanged.

## Design
- Signature becomes `render(user, options = {})`.
- Greeting is `"Dear"` when `options.formal === true`, else `"Hi"` (anything else — omitted, `{}`, `{ formal: false }` — behaves exactly like today).
- Interpolation and all other behavior stay identical; no output changes for existing callers.

## Changes
1. `lib/render.mjs`
   - Accept a second options argument defaulting to `{}` and select the greeting word from `options.formal`.
2. `tests/render.test.mjs`
   - Keep the existing "informal greeting" test exactly as is.
   - Add tests: `render({name}, { formal: true })` → `"Dear ada"`; `render({name})` (no second arg) → `"Hi ada"`; `render({name}, { formal: false })` → `"Hi ada"`; `render({name}, {})` → `"Hi ada"`.

## Order of work
1. Modify `lib/render.mjs`.
2. Extend `tests/render.test.mjs`.
3. Run `node --test`; the pre-existing test plus new tests must all pass before declaring done.

## Done when
- Formal mode works via the options argument.
- One-argument behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged and the original test passes untouched.
- Full suite green.
